summary: Adolfo Velazquez is CTO and co-founder of ROSE Diagnostics (Carlsbad, CA, incorporated 2023). The company is building the verifi LUNG Test, a 5-minute point-of-care cartridge-and-reader device that tells clinicians during a lung biopsy whether the specimen is sufficient for analysis. He is a genuine diagnostics insider who led Quidel SOFIA rapid tests, but this is an in-vitro diagnostic hardware company with no evidence of AI or software, so it falls outside Example Seed Fund's AI-native software thesis.

company.what_they_build: verifi LUNG Test: a portable, roughly 5-minute rapid test (collection vial, test cartridge and small reader) that confirms during a lung biopsy whether the collected specimen is sufficient for analysis. company.customers: Intended for clinicians and clinics performing lung biopsies (S4). No paying customers are evidenced; the product is pre-clearance with a clinical study that enrolled its first patient Dec 2024 (S4).

thesis_fit.belief: Compliance and auditability are the moat in regulated AI, not the model
thesis_fit.evidence: There is no AI product. The defensibility appears to come from FDA device clearance and, per a data-provider profile, proprietary engineered antibodies and a biomarker panel, not from software audit trails.

thesis_fit.belief: Founders from inside the industry beat generalists who discover it later
thesis_fit.evidence: Velazquez led multiple Quidel SOFIA point-of-care tests to commercialization, and co-founders come from i-STAT and medical-device regulatory roles. Their expertise is in diagnostics hardware, though, not regulated software.

thesis_fit.belief: Open-source or public traction is the best early signal for technical founders
thesis_fit.evidence: No GitHub, Hacker News, papers or other public technical output appear in the evidence.

thesis_fit.belief: Small teams shipping weekly beat large early rounds
thesis_fit.evidence: Individual rounds are modest ($1M to $2.7M). However, the company is a hardware device in clinical study awaiting FDA clearance, with no sign of weekly software shipping.

strengths: Deep, specific point-of-care diagnostics track record: led five Quidel SOFIA tests to market (S5).
Experienced founding team with a prior exit-linked product (i-STAT CHEM8+, Abbott $392M acquisition) and in-house FDA and Health Canada regulatory expertise (S5).
Clear clinical problem: the site says up to 40% of lung biopsy samples are returned as insufficient (S4).
Steady progress: prototype (2024), first clinical study patient (Dec 2024), development milestone (Aug 2025) (S4).
Repeat investor base of 18 in each Form D filing (S3).
risks: Off-thesis: this is an in-vitro diagnostic hardware device (cartridge and reader), not AI-native software. No AI or software component is evidenced (S4, S2).
Not FDA cleared or approved in any jurisdiction, so there is a long and capital-intensive regulatory path ahead (S4).

Sources disagree on amounts: the shortlist record (S1) attaches $2,344,375 sold to the 2026-09-15 filing, but the Form D list (S3) shows that figure on the 2025-05-13 filing and $2,208,750 on the 2026 filing.
Site amounts do not match filings exactly: the July 2026 news cites $2.7M raised, but the 2026 Form D shows $2,208,750 sold. The $1M 2024 seed has no matching Form D among the 2 filings (S1, S3, S4).
The website was guessed from the company name. Founder names on the About page match the Form D people list, so it is very likely the same company, but this should be confirmed (S1, S5).
Several news pages returned no content (S6, S7, S8), so milestone details are unverified.
open_questions: Does the verifi LUNG reader include any software, data capture or algorithmic interpretation, or is the readout purely assay-based?
What FDA pathway (510(k), De Novo, PMA) are you pursuing for verifi LUNG, and what is the timeline to submission?
What has the clinical study that enrolled its first patient in Dec 2024 shown so far on sensitivity and specificity for specimen sufficiency?
How does the verifi LUNG platform build on what you learned shipping the Quidel SOFIA tests, and is it designed to extend to other biopsy types?
Can you reconcile the $2.7M announced in July 2026 with the $2.21M sold on the 2026 Form D, and what is total capital needed to clearance?
Who is the economic buyer: interventional pulmonology, the hospital lab, or the procedure suite?
conversation_openers: Your work taking Quidel's SOFIA tests from concept to market looks directly relevant to verifi LUNG. I'd love to hear how a 5-minute in-procedure sufficiency check changes the lung biopsy workflow.
The stat that up to 40% of lung biopsy samples come back insufficient caught my eye. How are you thinking about data and reporting around the verifi LUNG result once it's in the procedure room?
Congrats on the 2026 round and the clinical study progress since your first patient in Dec 2024. Curious whether there's a software or analytics layer on the roadmap.
